title: Deep-learning-enabled antibiotic discovery through molecular de-extinction
summary: Deep-learning-enabled antibiotic discovery through molecular de-extinction. Deep-learning ensembles scored 10,311,899 peptides from extinct-organism proteomes for antimicrobial activity and prioritized candidates for synthesis. 69 peptides were synthesized and tested against bacterial pathogens per the abstract; most killed bacteria by membrane depolarization. Evidence limits: In vivo and mechanistic details beyond the abstract were not assessed; clinical relevance is not established. Reviewed from Europe PMC abstract only.
ai_technology: Peptide-sequence encoder plus neural-network ensembles (APEX-type) mining extinct-organism proteomes
organization: Machine Biology Group, Departments of Psychiatry and Microbiology, Institute for Biomedical Informatics, Institute for Translational Medicine and Therapeutics, Perelman School of Medicine, University
